A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the Morpheus benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization and some internal reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: v1 reports original recordings of physical experiments and evaluations of generated videos, including quantitative scores in Figures 6–8 and Tables A5–A10.

after.justification: v2 reports original physical experiments, evaluations of additional video generators, and original-versus-augmented conditioning results in Figures 6–8 and 16–24.

M1.justification: v2 adds a substantive augmentation stage before video conditioning: COSMOS-Transfer1 generates appearance variants using SAM2 masks, manual screening and optional Canny guidance (Section 3, Appendix B). v1 conditions directly on recorded videos. The core trajectory extraction and PINN/invariance scoring procedures remain largely unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds rolling, sliding, collisions and spring oscillation, expands falling to additional everyday objects, and evaluates stylized conditioning across five experiment types (Appendices A–B). Non-holonomic pendulum descriptions disappear, but its results remain in Figures 16–21; it therefore cannot be counted as an unambiguous coverage removal.

E2.justification: COSMOS-predict2 and WAN-2.1 join the four retained model families in the main comparisons; v1's COSMOS corresponds to COSMOS-predict1. Figure 14 additionally reports Veo3 and Veo3-fast depth consistency, although Appendix D.2 excludes them from the final analysis. That figure also omits v1 Figure A7's real-world reference bar.

E3.justification: v2 adds original-versus-augmented evaluation and changes aggregate reporting to select the better plain/enhanced-prompt result (Section 5). Figure 7 introduces a combined score averaging Dynamical and Physical Invariance scores, whereas v1 reports them separately. New models receive specified generation settings; retained PINN training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 22 adds a substantive robustness analysis testing sensitivity to appearance-transferred conditioning, which v1 does not examine. Prompting and failure-mode analyses are updated. Existing energy and pendulum case studies largely remain, while v1 Figure A9's paired projectile and non-holonomic trajectory examples are removed.

E5.justification: No new seed-based replication, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are reported. The repeated-recording description, invariant time-series variability calculations and shaded energy examples are retained; these do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 reports extensive new or replaced results: Figure 7 gives WAN-2.1 keyframe interpolation a total score of 0.55 and COSMOS-predict2 scores of 0.43 for single-frame and 0.52 for multi-frame conditioning. Appearance-sensitivity results are added, while v1's detailed per-prompt and per-invariant tables are removed. Changed coverage and aggregation prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 Table 3 adds assumptions and conserved quantities for sliding, rolling, elastic collisions and spring systems. The non-holonomic invariance discussion in v1 Appendix C.4 is removed. The retained PINN losses, differentiation formulas, score scaling and pendulum derivations are essentially unchanged; no new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a real-video physics benchmark, complementary invariance and equation-of-motion evaluations, and evidence that visually realistic generators violate physical laws despite improved conditioning. Expanded evaluations and the reformulated contribution list support the same central scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands limitations to address evaluator mismatch from unmodeled forces, uncalibrated 2D trajectories, tracking errors, static cameras and short clips (Section 6, Appendix E). It also recasts stillness as addressed by existing filtering instead of a future penalty, and removes much of v1's detailed interpretation of individual conservation metrics.

D1.justification: v2 documents augmentation screening, mask reuse and optional 0.5/0.5 edge-and-mask conditioning, plus setups and prompts for the added experiments. Table 4 adds model parameter counts and new-model hyperparameters, and the reproducibility statement specifies GitHub and Hugging Face destinations. Conversely, non-holonomic setup and prompt documentation is removed despite retained results.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to COSMOS-Transfer1, WAN and Qwen2-VL, and elaborates its critique of trajectory matching and Physics-IQ's variance normalization. The principal related-work coverage and positioning around physics-law evaluation remain stable; reference reordering and formatting are presentation changes.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introductory motivation, dataset narrative and prompting explanation. Experiment descriptions move into the appendix, the detailed additional-analysis narrative is compressed, and augmentation, extended limitations and disclosure sections reorganize the appendices. Author information and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column layout, redraws the overview, merges v1 Figures 4–5 into its Figure 4, and relocates the benchmark-comparison table. Detailed result tables and scatterplots give way to aggregated bars and heatmaps, alongside new experiment and augmentation montages. These are extensive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Broader physical coverage, the new appearance-robustness experiment and explicit evaluator-mismatch limitations strengthen v2. However, it loses v1's detailed diagnostic tables and inconsistently specifies evaluated coverage: non-holonomic results remain in Figures 16–21 despite omission from the dataset and method descriptions. These tradeoffs leave the interpretation and auditability of the new aggregate findings insufficiently clear for a reliable net quality judgment.
